alakazam._bench_note: bench_target stays at the class default 3. Raising it to 4 (the live agents hold 3.25) measured WORSE on both decks -- hand at Powerful Hand 11.71->11.37 and 11.30->11.00, win 50->48 and 62->60. Benching a Pokemon COSTS a card from hand, and this deck's damage IS 20 x hand size, so every extra body is -20 damage. The live 3.25 bench is a CONSEQUENCE of them drawing more, not a cause.
alakazam._line_note: card_roles order Abra/Kadabra=engine(705) > Dunsparce/Dudunsparce=line(605) > Alakazam=win(905). Reason: _card_need = tier + usefulness//10, and Dawn picks a Basic / a Stage 1 / a Stage 2 by that score. BEFORE: Abra 605 == Dunsparce 605 (a COIN FLIP for the Basic) and Kadabra 605 < Dudunsparce 705 (the Stage-1 pick took the draw engine, not the line). AFTER: line 82% Kadabra in losses (was 71%), Abra 98% (was 93%), Dawn 1.75/g (live 1.77). BUT this is a WASH, not a win: Alakazam-in-play in losses moved only 76% -> 77%, alakazam hand at Powerful Hand got WORSE 11.56 -> 10.79 and win stayed 50%; nz_fez improved 62 -> 66%. Kept because win >= before on both decks. NOTE the tension: Dudunsparce draws 3 and this deck's damage IS 20 x hand size, so the engine outranking the line may have been RIGHT -- the fix trades hand size for line consistency.

black_kyurem._dawn_note: Do NOT add draw_supporters=[Dawn 1231] to the decks that run Dawn. Tested on all 10 of them at matched 150 games/opponent: the 5 where Dawn actually started firing (black_kyurem 1.35/g, mega_heracross 1.22, hydreigon 0.95, marnie_grimmsnarl 0.66, zangoose 0.60) averaged +0.84pt -- and the other 5, where Dawn went 0.00 -> 0.00 and the pilot did not change AT ALL, averaged +0.72pt while swinging -3.8 to +4.2. That unchanged cohort IS the noise floor of the experiment, and the effect is inside it. Dawn only paid off on alakazam because it was paired with draw_threshold=30, which is only justified where the damage IS the hand size (Powerful Hand = 20 x hand). Here the default draw_threshold=5 gate blocks it anyway.

dragapult._migration_note: NOT on ConfigL2: its `need` is a COUNT, and Phantom Dive (154) costs [2,5] = {R}+{P}, a two-TYPE cost. `need:{121:2}` is satisfied by any 2 energy, so the deck always had a payable Jet Headbutt (cost [0]) and led with it -- Phantom Dive 48.5% (legacy) -> 24.1% (config), i.e. the deck stopped being a spread deck. archetype='spread' -> SpreadPolicy restores it: Phantom Dive back in the lead (36.5%) and winrate 44.5 -> 51.2 at 150 games/opp. GAP: the line config has no vocabulary for typed needs.

dudunsparce_box._note: scouted 2026-08-05 top-500: the cluster that holds ranks 6 and 9, whose 60/60 reconstructions are IDENTICAL. 13 teams matched nothing of ours above 41%, and a further 14 classified as mega_lopunny at only 59-65% carry the same engine -- so our mega_lopunny is a DIFFERENT deck from the live one. See docs/meta/leaderboard_top500_2026-08-05.md
dudunsparce_box._plan: Dudunsparce is a REUSABLE draw engine: its ability draws 3 and then shuffles itself back into the deck, so the Dunsparce line is dug up again and again (Buddy-Buddy Poffin / Poke Pad / Ultra Ball all fetch it). The payoff is Mega Lopunny ex's Gale Thrust -- 60, +170 MORE if it moved from the Bench to the Active Spot this turn, i.e. 230 for one Energy -- which is why Air Balloon x3 (-2 retreat) is in here: retreat something cheap, drop Lopunny in, swing. Mega Froslass ex is the second angle, 50 per card in the opponent's HAND. Mist Energy protects the Mega from attack EFFECTS and Battle Cage protects the bench from spread.
dudunsparce_box._tuning: CONFIG-ONLY pass 1, measured. Gale Thrust landed 60 rather than 230 on 95.2% of its 83 uses (the +170 needs Lopunny to have moved Bench->Active THAT turn, and the engine parks it Active instead), while Mega Froslass ex's Resentful Refrain averaged 308 damage over its 6 uses. The engine already prices 'for each card in your opponent's hand' correctly (engine_v2:_ctx_each_count), so this is a PRIORITY problem, not a valuation one: Froslass is now the primary focus and Lopunny the secondary. PASS 2: the L2 pivot beat config-only by +4.37pt +- 1.96 (t +2.23, 640 games) but the mechanism check said the Gale Thrust window only went 3.5% -> 7.4%, so the gain was NOT the pivot. The real blocker is upstream: a benched Lopunny never gets energy, so there is nothing to pivot into. line.support_energy arms it on the bench (engine_v2:_support_attach), which is what that key exists for. PASS 3: promoting FROSLASS instead of Lopunny (Gale Thrust was 226 uses at a 6.2% window, i.e. a 60; Resentful Refrain averaged 240) took the deck 26.4% -> 45.0% and the paired gap over config-only to +9.53pt +- 2.24 (t +4.26). PASS 4 tried true-damage attack selection and a wall-aware Spiky Hopper line: the first never fired (one energy leaves Refrain the only legal attack) and the second was +0.3pt over 640 games. Both REVERTED.

ogerpon_mono._plan: Mono-attacker turbo. FOUR Pokemon in the whole deck, all Teal Mask Ogerpon ex. Its ability attaches a Basic {G} from hand AND draws, so the deck is 17 Basic {G} + 2 Grow Grass feeding one body; Myriad Leaf Shower is 30 + 30 per Energy on BOTH Actives, so damage scales with the pile it has built. Everything else is draw (Judge / Lillie's / Harlequin), search (Tera Orb finds it -- Ogerpon is Tera), or survivability (Lively Stadium +30 to Basics, Grow Grass +20, Hero's Cape +100, Jumbo Ice Cream heals 80 at 3+ Energy).
